title: (In caubeen with clay pipe stuck in the band, dusty brogues, an emigrant’s red handkerchief bundle in his hand, leading a black bogoak pig by a sugaun, with a smile in his eye.)
html_source: Gifford/Seidman help us with this: a caubeen is an old, shabby cap, a bogoak is a piece of ancient oak preserved in a peat bog, and a sugaun is Irish for a rope made of twisted hay or straw. A “smile in the eye” refers to a phrase in Thomas Moore’s poem Erin, the Tear and the Smile in Thine Eyes in his Irish Melodies. The whole thing is to caricaturize Bloom as the “stage Irishman.”
